tasks.commitBody:
A signed file URL lives 60 seconds and must never be cached — Entu's own rule, quoted at the signing site — so the only thing that can survive a rehearsal with no signal is the bytes. Opening a part now reads through an identity-partitioned byte store: hit serves stored bytes as a blob URL; miss mints a fresh signed URL, fetches, stores, serves. The signed URL itself is never persisted, and the popup-blocker-safe synchronous tab-open survives in all three handlers (agenda, event, library — the event page also gains the error surface it never had, reusing the existing message keys; zero new locale strings).

Staleness is structural, probe-settled on polyphony (ledgers cited at the site): no Entu replace path — documented DELETE+POST, or POST-with-existing-_id, which file properties turn into an append — ever lets the same file-property _id serve different bytes, so keying on the _id makes a replaced file an automatic miss with no validator logic. The bucket's CORS admits fetch from mvox.eu today (probe-verified; no infrastructure change needed for the read leg) but exposes no headers, so client-side ETag comparison is recorded as a future infrastructure ask rather than built; #333's hash-pin hook is served by an app-computed digest of the fetched bytes, stored as metadata.

Partitioning follows Gama's ruling on the issue: keys are (database, person-id, file-id) with identity captured at request-issue time — a fetch that settles after a collective switch stores under the identity that started it and never poisons the new one — and an anonymous session can construct no key at all, which is what makes another identity's bytes unreachable rather than merely evictable. The store is RETAINED across logout by keeping it out of the auth teardown entirely (token expiry calls the same path, and delete-on-logout would have the cache destroyed by a routine invisible event); the partition is stated in code as a correctness boundary, not a security one; a clearPartition operation ships now, its member-facing control belongs to #334. The cap is global with least-recently-opened eviction across partitions. fake-indexeddb enters devDependencies for the adapter tests; runtime dependencies remain zero.

Closes #343
